findings.reason: the plan's own §4 sign-convention/equation/symbol checks should cite the existing owner and either extend it or say in one line why its rules cannot be reused, per the reuse-item contract.
findings.text: §4's five conformance check classes are proposed as new, but imas_codex/standard_names/docs_gates.py already implements three of them deterministically and is nowhere named in the plan's prior-art account

findings.reason: the honest change is to extend docs_gates.py and route `score_documentation` into the Layer 1 audit report the reviewer reads, not to write a second sign-convention check.
findings.text: §4's fifth check class, "a sign-convention paragraph present or absent against the COCOS rule", duplicates `_sign_convention_result`, which already decides sign prose exactly from authoritative COCOS transformation type (fail on a COCOS-invariant quantity that states a sign, fail on a COCOS-sensitive quantity that omits or misplaces it); the plan forks this into review/audits.py rather than extending the owner

findings.reason: the same module the plan routes §4's checks past (because score_documentation is unwired) already holds the equation gate; the plan should name it and decide extend-vs-wire rather than add a third equation check.
findings.text: §4's first check class, a forbidden variant of a registered concept's equation, duplicates `_defining_equation_result` in the same owner module, which already gates documentation on its defining equation and dimensional consistency

findings.reason: §4 should extend the existing symbol gate with the registry's per-quantity canonical symbol rather than add a parallel symbol check; the registry supplies the canonical symbol the owner currently lacks, which is the extension argument.
findings.text: §4's second check class, a non-canonical symbol for a registered quantity, duplicates `_symbols_are_defined` in the same owner module, which already gates documentation on symbol definition

findings.reason: naming that the locus-gloss check extends the existing `convention_violation` family (rather than forming a fifth class) lets the author reuse the report shape and the reviewer's existing rendering path instead of introducing a parallel finding class.

findings.reason: the anti-pattern gallery is keyed on name decomposition while concepts.yml is keyed on description/documentation content, so the mechanisms do not in fact overlap; a one-line "distinct from the decomposition gallery in anti_patterns.yaml" would remove the doubt but the design does not change.
findings.text: the plan's concepts.yml "forbidden variants as patterns" and templates.yml openings are curated wrong-form→canonical maps, the same shape as the shipped anti-pattern gallery (anti_patterns.yaml, loaded by context.py:372 `_load_decomposition_anti_patterns`), which the plan neither names nor distinguishes
